stories.title: Former councillor murdered on morning walk in Gorakhpur:Ran 100 metres after attack, 4 men chased stabbed him
stories.summary: A former councillor was murdered while out on a morning walk in Gorakhpur. According to eyewitnesses, 4 attackers surrounded him and launched a knife attack. After being assaulted, former councillor Rajkumar Chauhan tried to escape and ran nearly 100 metres. However, the attackers chased him and stabbed him again. They repeatedly attacked him in the chest, head and hands. Eyewitnesses said the assailants waited at the spot for some time to ensure he had died before fleeing the scene. Family members rushed Rajkumar Chauhan to BRD Medical College, where doctors declared him dead. Initial reports suggest the attackers had parked their vehicle some distance away and reached the crime scene on foot. After receiving information about the incident, police reached the spot and began scanning CCTV footage from the surrounding areas. The incident took place in the Bargadwa area under the limits of Chiluatal Police Station. See images related to the incident- Rajkumar was only brother of 4 sisters Rajkumar Chauhan's father is Jangi Chauhan. Rajkumar was their only son. He had four sisters, all of whom are married. Rajkumar got married 18 years ago. He has two daughters and a son. He was preparing to contest the assembly elections in 2027. A youth said - Brother Rajkumar Chauhan has been shot. He was going to contest the assembly elections in 2027. When we used to meet him daily, we would discuss which places to go for campaigning.

stories.title: UP police officials clarify ‘Pandit’ option not a crime:Sub-Inspector exam paper not to be re-conducted; results to be released on time
stories.summary: Politics has intensified over the inclusion of the ‘Pandit’ option for opportunists in the UP Sub-Inspector recruitment exam, raising questions about action against those responsible. However, the recruitment board and its former officials believe no major action is likely, neither will the company be blacklisted nor treated as a criminal case, and results are expected on time. CM Yogi had directed the Police Recruitment Board to investigate the entire process, but no action has been taken so far. An investigation by Dainik Bhaskar examined the agency conducting the exam and identified the three key individuals responsible for adding the ‘Pandit’ option. First - Chairman of the Recruitment Board Second - Exam Controller of the Recruitment Board Third - Exam Conducting Agency Rules made in 2008, process kept confidential to prevent leaks After speaking with board officials, it came to light that the Chairman and the Examination Controller are not being held responsible for such irregularities. How is this possible? We spoke to Satyarth Aniruddha Pankaj, DIG of the Recruitment Board, about this. He says- Orders have been given to investigate the controversy that has arisen regarding the question. I want to state that the Police Recruitment Board does not set its own papers. It gets this work done by confidential agencies. To prevent paper leaks, no officer or employee of the board can see the paper. The sealed packets of the paper are opened for the first time at the center in the presence of 2 candidates. Action will be taken only after the investigation into the question and its options, which are causing controversy, is completed. Will the agency be blacklisted? Candidates are asking whether the agency conducting the UP Sub-Inspector exam will be blacklisted. Officials say the issue is not serious enough for that. Former DGP Sulkhan Singh adds that technically, there is no error in the question; it is being exaggerated, no crime has been committed, and results will be released on time. The recruitment board’s ongoing investigation report is still awaited. The exam will not be re-conducted, but a new SOP will be created to avoid questions on religion, caste, or community that may hurt sentiments. How is the agency that sets the paper decided? The recruitment board conducts a confidential tender process, inviting agencies from across the country and selecting one internally. Former DGP Sulkhan Singh says the paper-setting process is highly confidential, and even the board does not know the questions in advance. How do agencies prepare questions? Agencies hire subject matter experts. For 100 questions, around 200 are collected from different experts and used to prepare four sets of papers. Questions cover General Hindi, General Knowledge, Numerical and Mental Ability, and Law and Constitution, following the syllabus. Each question and its options are carefully checked for accuracy and clarity. How to ensure security during printing The question about 'Pandit Vikalp' is at the center of the controversy The question in the exam asked candidates to choose a word for someone who changes according to the occasion. The options were Virtuous, Pandit, Opportunist, and Sincere. An official linked to the recruitment board said it was a multiple-choice question, not a synonym question. In such questions, three options are usually incorrect, so linking the word ‘Pandit’ with ‘opportunist’ is not justified. However, the Brahmin community, BJP MLAs, and leaders strongly objected to including ‘Pandit’ as an option. They said the term is associated with knowledge, scholarship and religious respect, and linking it to opportunism insults the dignity of the community. Why did politics heat up? The controversy has also turned political. BJP leaders, including Deputy CM Brajesh Pathak, and MLAs Shalabhmani Tripathi, P.N. Pathak, and Ramesh Mishra, objected to the question. Some issued statements, while others wrote letters to the Chief Minister demanding action. Senior journalist Siddharth Kalahans said the issue gained political traction because it surfaced at a time when many Brahmins already feel their identity is being hurt. He cited recent controversies involving BJP MLA meetings, UGC matters, the “corrupt Pandit” remark, Shankaracharya, and incidents like pulling the topknot of young Brahmins. As a result, BJP leaders raised the issue and wrote to the Chief Minister to control the damage, after which the CM termed the question wrong and ordered an investigation. stories.title: By-elections on 3 UP Assembly seats after April 10:Pending SIR list causes the delay; SP says, 'BJP is scared'
stories.summary: By-elections for three assembly seats in Uttar Pradesh could be held after April 10. According to Election Commission officials, polls cannot be conducted during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of the electoral rolls, so elections can only take place after the final voter list is released. The Election Commission had announced assembly elections for Assam, Kerala, Puducherry, Tamil Nadu and West Bengal on March 15, but did not declare dates for the UP by-elections. This triggered speculation that the polls for the three seats had been postponed. Experts say the commission currently has two options: By-elections are due for the Ghosi, Faridpur and Dudhi assembly seats. For Faridpur, the BJP has indicated it may field the son of its current MLA, Dr. Shyam Bihari. Meanwhile, the Samajwadi Party is preparing to nominate family members of the MLAs in Ghosi and Dudhi, aiming to use the sympathy factor. The SP is considered strong on both these seats. This raises key questions: Can the Election Commission postpone the by-elections? Which faces from the BJP and SP are likely to contest the three seats? And what preparations are both parties making for the upcoming contests? Read in this report Rules for by-elections Under the rules of the Election Commission of India, by-elections should be held within 6 months of a seat becoming vacant. There are 2 conditions for this- 1. If the term of the assembly seat remaining is more than 6 months, then by-elections are held. 2. According to Section 151 of the Representation of the People Act, the commission should conduct by-elections within 6 months if a seat becomes vacant. BJP, SP's preparations BJP leaders busy with Bengal elections After the announcement of West Bengal election dates, the BJP organisation is preparing to send several leaders there for campaigning, including CM Yogi, Deputy CM Keshav Prasad Maurya and Brajesh Pathak. Meanwhile, the party’s local cadre is doing public outreach in the constituencies. Potential candidates have also been asked to connect with people and strengthen their political presence. SP leaders active, want by-elections soon SP leaders, on the other hand, want by-elections for all three seats to be held soon. The party sees these polls as a semi-final before the 2027 UP assembly elections. While the results may not significantly impact the assembly polls, they could influence the political atmosphere. SP leaders believe there is resentment among upper-caste voters against the BJP and want to test this factor in these elections. BSP not active; its entry may hurt SP more It is believed that the by-elections will mainly see a direct contest between SP and BJP. However, if the BSP fields candidates, it could hurt SP more than BJP. At present, BSP’s cadre does not appear active on any of the three seats. Words of BJP, SP leaders Victory on all three seats is certain BJP State Spokesperson Hero Bajpai says, The Election Commission of India decides the date for the by-election. BJP will contest the election with full might. It is certain that only BJP candidates will win on all three seats, including Duddhi and Ghosi. On the ground, our workers are active among the people. They are continuously reaching out to people and informing them about the work done during BJP's rule. SP leaders are feeling insecure. BJP is afraid of defeat SP's national spokesperson Ameeq Jamei says, BJP has already started fearing defeat. That's why they don't want to hold by-elections. In fact, BJP is troubled by the increasing strength of PDA. They know that if elections are held now, they will not be able to win even by using all means, fair or foul. stories.title: Cricketer Rinku Singh offers prayers in Mathura:Visits Baglamukhi Devi temple, says ‘won the World Cup with the mother’s blessings’
stories.summary: Star cricketer Rinku Singh arrived in Mathura on Monday following India’s victory in the T20 World Cup 2026. He visited the Maa Baglamukhi Devi Temple, where he offered prayers and sought blessings. Speaking after the visit, Rinku said, “I had prayed for the team to win the World Cup. With the blessings of Maa Baglamukhi, we achieved victory.” He remained at the temple for around 45 minutes. BJP leader Yogesh Dwivedi accompanied him during the visit. India defeated New Zealand by 96 runs in the final held in Ahmedabad on 8 March. During the tournament, Rinku suffered a personal loss, as his father, Khanchand Singh, passed away. He had briefly returned to Aligarh to perform the last rites. See 2 pictures- Felicitation and temple rituals Before heading to the temple, Rinku visited the farmhouse of former municipal president Pushpa Sharma in Chhatikara. There, he was honoured with a shawl by Pushpa Sharma and Yogesh Dwivedi. Both congratulated him and the Indian team on their World Cup victory. At around noon, Rinku reached the temple near the old bus stand, where priest Neeraj Chaturvedi guided him through the rituals. He offered flowers, presented bhog (food offering), and lit a ceremonial lamp. Priests conducted a special puja with Vedic chants. During the ceremony, Rinku prayed for his family’s well-being and the prosperity of the nation. A large crowd gathered outside the temple to catch a glimpse of the cricketer. After completing the rituals, Rinku interacted with fans and posed for photographs. He expressed gratitude, saying that he had received immense love from people across the country and especially from the Braj region, adding that he would always cherish this support. Uttar Pradesh Ranji team player Ansh Dwivedi was also present. Later, Rinku visited a fuel station, where Indian Oil’s regional officer Lucky Gautam welcomed him with a bouquet. World Cup journey and performance Rinku Singh had not been part of the main squad during the 2024 World Cup and was included as a travelling reserve. However, he earned a place in the 2026 T20 World Cup squad, marking his debut in the tournament. He played five matches during the competition, scoring a total of 24 runs. Personal loss during the tournament Rinku’s father, Khanchand Singh, passed away on 27 February at 4:36 am in Aligarh. He had been battling stage-four liver cancer and was 60 years old. Rinku returned home for the funeral but rejoined Team India immediately afterwards. Following the World Cup victory, he shared an emotional message on Instagram- ‘Dad, today the trophy is in my hands, but you are not with me. Your dream has come true.’ He added that he would miss his father in every moment of joy and that his father’s teachings about duty had guided him on the field. Wedding plans with Priya Saroj Rinku Singh is engaged to Samajwadi Party MP Priya Saroj. Their wedding is scheduled for 2026, with earlier dates having been postponed twice, first due to a cricket series and then because of the World Cup. Sources indicate the wedding may now take place in May, depending on Rinku’s availability after the IPL season, expected between 26 March and 31 May. The ceremony is planned in Kashi, with a reception in Aligarh.

stories.title: Deputy CM Brajesh Pathak stands in line as patient:Spends an hour at Lucknow CHC, fumes over poor hygiene
stories.summary: Deputy Chief Minister Brajesh Pathak carried out a surprise inspection at Chinhat Community Health Centre (CHC) in Lucknow on Monday. To assess the situation firsthand, he wore a mask and joined the queue as an ordinary patient. He obtained an OPD slip and stood in line at both the pathology and medicine distribution counters. For nearly close to an hour, no one recognised him. During this time, he closely observed the functioning of the hospital and was visibly displeased with the level of cleanliness. Action over poor hygiene Disturbed by the unhygienic conditions, Pathak ordered a week’s payment of the cleaning agency to be withheld. He instructed officials that no staff member would be allowed to leave until the premises were properly cleaned. He also reprimanded the concerned officers for failing to maintain basic cleanliness standards in the hospital. Now see 3 pictures- Anger over ward conditions During the inspection, the Deputy CM expressed strong displeasure over the condition of the wards. Several beds in the general ward were found without bedsheets, and overall cleanliness was lacking. He warned officials that negligence in patient care would not be tolerated. Notices were ordered to be issued to those responsible, and strict action was promised if conditions did not improve promptly. Review of pathology and facilities Pathak then visited the pathology department, where he noticed a long queue of patients. He asked the technician about the time required to collect a blood sample and directed that the process be expedited to reduce waiting time. Dust and dirt were also observed near the X-ray room, prompting immediate instructions for cleaning. He further inspected supplies by opening a cupboard and checking the stock available. Inspection of OPD and general ward In OPD Room No. 5, the Deputy CM spoke with doctors about patient load and hospital arrangements. Upon reaching General Ward No. 28, he was angered by the conditions, beds without sheets and poor hygiene. He also inspected the toilets and directed officials to ensure immediate improvement in sanitation facilities. Issues in drinking water facilities The inspection revealed shortcomings in drinking water arrangements as well. Dirt was found around the RO system, and pipes were improperly tied with a net. Expressing dissatisfaction, Pathak emphasised that there would be no compromise on cleanliness and essential facilities in the hospital. Concerns raised by ASHA workers During the visit, ASHA workers undergoing training in the auditorium informed him that their mobile phones were not functioning, affecting their work. In response, the Deputy CM immediately contacted Chief Medical Officer Dr. NB Singh and instructed that the devices be repaired or replaced without delay. He also directed that any pending payments to ASHA workers be cleared promptly. Strict instructions to officials Pathak instructed the CMO to reach the CHC immediately and resolve all issues. He warned officials not to leave the hospital until all arrangements were fully corrected. Observing a long queue at the medicine counter, he directed the CHC Superintendent to streamline the process, stating that patients should receive medicines within five minutes.

stories.title: BJP groups clash in Aligarh:12 bullets fired, three shot in market area
stories.summary: A violent clash broke out between two groups linked to the Bharatiya Janata Party in Aligarh, Uttar Pradesh. The groups opened fire at each other in a busy market, and 3 people were injured. 12 rounds fired in 23 seconds The incident took place on March 12 in Sarai Hakim market. According to police, around 12 rounds were fired within just 23 seconds, causing panic and chaos in the area. A video of the incident surfaced on Thursday. So far, 13 accused have been arrested and sent to jail. Police are using the video to identify other suspects. See 2 pictures Fight started over Instagram reel Police said the clash began over an argument on Instagram. Harshad Hindu and Mahesh Sharma, both associated with the BJP youth wing, had a dispute after a comment was made on a reel. The argument escalated into abuse over a phone call and later turned violent. One group allegedly assaulted a person named Mohit Sharma earlier, which further increased tensions. Gunfight in market area On the evening of March 12, both groups gathered again in the market and opened fire at each other. In the video, one injured person can be seen falling on the road while others try to help him. Attackers were also seen firing from narrow lanes. Three injured, some arrested Three people were injured in the firing: Police later arrested injured accused Shoaib Ahmad and Shanu Valmiki after their treatment and sent them to jail. Search for main accused continues Police said the accused had gathered on Harshad’s call. They are now searching for main suspects, including Mohit Sharma, Aman Pandit, Prakhar Rathi, and Mannu Pandit. SP City Mrigank Shekhar Pathak said that strict action will be taken, and illegal activities linked to both groups will also be investigated.

stories.title: UP Evening Wrap:‘No tolerance for disruption during festivals’ warns CM Yogi; BJP releases second list for WB assembly elections more
stories.summary: Bhaskar English brings you the biggest news from Uttar Pradesh and around the world. Here are the top news headlines of the day: 1. BJP List 2 for WB polls out, former MoS Nisith Pramanik get tickets The Bharatiya Janata Party has announced candidates for 111 Assembly seats in West Bengal in its latest list. Rekha Patra, who did not contest from Sandeshkhali this time, has been fielded from Hingalganj. Former Union Minister of State for Home Affairs Nisith Pramanik has been nominated from Mathabhanga. 2. President Droupadi Murmu visits Ayodhya, offer prayers at Ram Temple President Droupadi Murmu visited the Ram Temple in Ayodhya on the first day of Navratri, where she offered prayers to Ram Lalla. She also installed the Shri Ram Yantra in the Ram Darbar located on the second floor and took a round of the temple premises. 3. Three departments responsible for Green Corridor road collapse The Green Corridor road sank 5 feet due to sewer leakage just 2 days after inauguration in Lucknow. The road caved in near Khatu Shyam Temple on Birbal Sahani Marg. LDA officials kept insisting this was part of the ramp adjacent to the Green Corridor. 4. Iran plans collecting tolls from shipping through Strait of Hormuz The US-Israel-Iran conflict has entered its 20th day, with both military and economic tensions escalating rapidly. A Washington Post report claims the Pentagon is seeking nearly $200 billion to sustain operations, signalling the growing cost of the war. 5. Will Varun Gandhi get a new role after meeting Modi?, absent from UP politics for two years Varun Gandhi entered politics and won the Pilibhit Lok Sabha seat in 2019. In 2014, he contested from Sultanpur and secured victory again by a margin of nearly 1.75 lakh votes. Just before the 2009 election, during a speech in Pilibhit, Varun made a controversial remark, stating that if anyone targeted Hindus or considered them leaderless, he would retaliate strongly, invoking the Gita. 6. ‘No tolerance for disruption during festivals’, says CM Yogi Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath said that no disturbance of any kind will be tolerated during festivals. Strict action will be taken against those who disrupt the atmosphere. Criminals should fear the police uniform. Festivals should be celebrated only within the bounds of tradition; no new traditions will be permitted. 7. Indian Railways crack down on unauthorised vendors Indian Railways has rolled out QR code-enabled identity cards and digitally traceable food packaging to eliminate unauthorised vending and ensure verified catering services onboard trains. Unauthorised hawking in passenger areas is prohibited and punishable under Section 144 of the Railways Act, 1989. 8. Supreme Court slams Barabanki toll clash; calls lawyer ‘brave’ who represented toll workers 'The behaviour of Barabanki Bar Association members is extremely sad and shameful. This is not the legal profession, but open hooliganism. This incident shows the declining state of the legal profession. Such violence can never be acceptable in the name of lawyers' fraternity (brotherhood).' This stern comment was made by the Supreme Court regarding a case related to a dispute at a toll plaza in Barabanki. 9. Army Major marries Captain bride by taking ₹1 as token-gift An Indian Army Major married a Captain (female) by taking just ₹1 as a token gift in Saharanpur. As per tradition, he only took one coconut. The groom said he had decided during his student life not to take a dowry. However, due to security reasons, information about where both are posted is not available. 10. Ajit Agarkar urges BCCI to extend tenure till 2027 WC Men's senior selection committee's chairman Ajit Agarkar is looking for another extension from BCCI after Team India successfully defended the T20 World Cup trophy at home this year on 8 March. Notably, after Men in Blue won the 2024 T20 World Cup and 2025 Champions Trophy, the Board of Control for Cricket in India rewarded the ex-cricketer with a one-year extension. For India's white-ball dominance, Agarkar's contract got extended from August 2025 to June 2026.

stories.title: 42-year-old man dies after jumping from 13th floor:Mother’s 3-day-old body found inside flat in Ghaziabad
stories.summary: A 42-year-old man died by suicide after jumping from the 13th floor of a residential building in Ghaziabad. When police later entered his flat, they found the body of his 70-year-old mother, which was believed to be 2–3 days old. The incident took place in the Mahagunpuram Society in the Kavinagar police station area. The man, identified as Rajveer Singh, lived in a ground-floor flat (No. 028). According to police, Rajveer first went to the 13th floor and then jumped through the duct area. He hit an iron shed on the way down and fell to the ground, seriously injured. A security guard nearby heard a loud noise and rushed to the spot. He found Rajveer lying in a pool of blood and raised an alarm, after which residents gathered and informed the police. First 2 pictures Mother’s body found inside flat When police entered Rajveer’s flat, they noticed a strong foul smell. Inside, they found the body of his mother, Satnam Kaur. Police said the body appeared to be around 2–3 days old, and no visible injury marks were found. Investigation ongoing Both bodies have been sent for postmortem to determine the exact cause of death. Police are investigating whether the mother died of natural causes and what led Rajveer to take this step. Family background Rajveer got married about 12 years ago. He was reportedly unemployed. His wife lives separately in Crossing Republic with their 10-year-old son. Local residents said they usually saw Rajveer coming and going, but his mother was rarely seen. Police are continuing the investigation to understand the full circumstances behind the incident.

stories.title: UP to hike salary of outsourced workers:Peons, translators and other staff see major payment boost
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh government, led by Yogi Adityanath, has increased the salaries of around 200,000 outsourcing employees. The salary hike ranges from ₹8,000 to ₹11,000. Major salary changes The revised salaries will be effective from April. Additional benefits introduced Apart from the salary increase, employees will now also receive: Budget allocation increased The Chief Minister had announced this decision in the Assembly. The government has increased the department’s budget by ₹426 crore, taking the total allocation to ₹2,223.84 crore. New corporation for transparent recruitment The government has also set up the Uttar Pradesh Outsource Service Corporation (UPCOS). From now on, all outsourcing recruitments in the state will be done through this body to ensure transparency. Earlier, different agencies handled hiring on a contract basis, which often led to exploitation of workers, delayed payments, and unfair wages. Reservation Policy to be implemented The government has also introduced reservation in outsourcing jobs: This move aims to ensure fair opportunities and address concerns raised by the opposition regarding lack of reservation in outsourcing jobs.

stories.title: Temple videos shared with Pakistan:2 youths caught in Hapur for espionage, SP confirms network active since 2025
stories.summary: Two young men have been arrested from Hapur district in Uttar Pradesh for allegedly spying for Pakistan. The arrests were made by a team of the Intelligence Bureau (IB) from Delhi. According to police, both suspects had been active since 2025. Police said the accused were in contact with a Pakistan-based gangster named Shahzad Bhatti through social media. They shared photos, videos, and locations of sensitive places, including temples and nearby areas. Hapur SP K.G. Singh stated that the accused—Azeem Rana and Azad Rajput—had sent videos of Sanatan Dharma Temple in Delhi, Ravana Temple in Greater Noida, and other nearby locations to their handler in Pakistan. Contact started via social media Investigations revealed that the contact began in 2025 through Instagram. Later, they also used Telegram and WhatsApp to stay connected. The accused were reportedly lured with money to share sensitive information. The police also found that they conducted reconnaissance (surveying) of places like Ramesh Nagar Metro Station, temples, and other public locations. On February 19, 2026, they shared multiple videos and photos. Family connection between accused Azeem Rana is from Dhaulana in Hapur, while Azad Rajput is from a village in Meerut. Azad is Azeem’s nephew. Their mobile phones contained several videos and images sent to the Pakistani handler. Case registered, investigation ongoing Police have registered a case against both accused and are questioning them further to uncover more details about the network. Who is Shahzad Bhatti? Shahzad Bhatti is believed to be a major gangster with links to international crime networks. He is reportedly involved in illegal arms trade and has connections across several countries, including Europe, the UK, the US, Canada, and Dubai. Reports suggest that he was once banned by the Pakistani government but later returned to Pakistan in May 2025. His exact current location is unknown.

stories.title: Elderly woman kept under digital arrest for 6 days:₹21 lakh duped; fraudsters say, 'You are involved with terrorists, your house will be sealed'
stories.summary: "This is Gujarat Police Commissioner speaking... 26 people lost their lives in a terrorist attack in Gujarat. Investigation has revealed that you are involved with militants and terrorists... You will be sent to jail, your house will be sealed... Until the investigation is complete, you must keep your mobile camera on; you have been digitally arrested... " Using such statements, cyber fraudsters digitally arrested an elderly woman from Kidwai Nagar for 6 days and swindled ₹21 lakh from her. Elderly woman lives alone after her husband's death Snehlata, a resident of Kidwai Nagar, said that she lives alone in a rented house. Her husband had passed away, and her son and daughter live elsewhere. She mentioned that some time ago, she had sold her LIG house in Vikas Sadan, Delhi and land in Krishnanagar, Kanpur, and the money received from these sales was deposited in her accounts. On the morning of March 10th, she received a call for the first time, where the caller threatened by mentioning involvement in a terrorist incident. After a while, they pressured her to accept a video call, saying they would send police to the house. When she answered the phone, a police officer appeared sitting in his office. He identified himself as the Gujarat Police Commissioner and spoke to them very rudely. ₹20 lakhs transferred from account on March 13th It is alleged that the fraudsters transferred ₹20 lakh from their State Bank of India account on March 13th. After this, on March 16th, they withdrew ₹50 thousand, ₹49 thousand, and ₹1 thousand through RTGS. Then the accused stopped calling. Snehlata said that they have a house in the city. There were talks about selling it. They had to go out regarding this matter. While the accused would stop them from going outside or having visitors, when they mentioned making a house deal for ₹80 lakhs, the accused let them go. Those people asked when the ₹80 lakhs would come, but she avoided answering. DCP Dipendra Nath Chaudhary said that a report has been filed. The matter is being investigated.

stories.title: Census from May 22; house counting in first phase:First-ever digital, caste census; self-enumeration option available
stories.summary: The first phase of the census will begin in Kanpur from May 22. House counting will be done from May 22 to June 20. During this time, it will be determined how many houses are in the district. Additionally, the second phase will begin in February 2027, in which citizens will be counted. For the first time, castes will also be observed in the census. Data will also be prepared showing how many citizens belong to each caste. Personnel engaged in the census will have to upload all data on the CMMS portal. For the first time in the country, the census is being conducted in digital format. Self-enumeration option for citizens for the first time DM Jitendra Pratap Singh said that in the first phase of the census, house listing and house counting will be done, and in the second phase, population counting will be conducted. He informed that this time's census will be completely digital and for the first time, citizens have been given the option of self-enumeration. He mentioned that 15 days prior to the census, citizens will be able to conduct their own enumeration through the Census Self-Enumeration Portal and app. Any ordinary resident can perform self-enumeration by filling out the online questionnaire. 33 details will be recorded During the house-listing phase, surveyors will record 33 types of details related to building usage, construction materials, number of rooms, ownership status, availability of water, electricity, and toilets, types of cooking fuel, and assets like phones, vehicles, and televisions.

stories.title: Army Major marries Captain bride by taking ₹1 as token-gift:Saharanpur groom says, 'I had decided in student life itself to have dowry-free marriage'
stories.summary: An Indian Army Major married a Captain (female) by taking just ₹1 as a token gift in Saharanpur. As per tradition, he only took one coconut. The groom said he had decided during his student life not to take a dowry. However, due to security reasons, information about where both are posted is not available. Meanwhile, the groom's father said that my son has not brought a daughter-in-law but a daughter. The brightness of our house has increased with the arrival of a daughter. We didn't want dowry anyway. What could be a bigger dowry than getting a daughter in the form of a daughter-in-law? This entire matter is from Meerpur village in the Sarsawa area. See 2 pictures of the wedding… The groom's family took ₹1 as token of blessing Chaudhary Ompal Singh, a resident of Meerpur village, has retired from the Indian Army. He is also the Joint Secretary of Sarsawa Arya Jat Samaj Development Committee. He conducted his son Madhur Chaudhary's marriage without dowry on March 16, 2026. Madhur got married to Jyoti Saurot from Brajmandal, where only ₹1 was taken as a token gift. Madhur's family members said that information related to his posting remains confidential, as permission is required from the army for this. Madhur was commissioned into the Indian Army after passing out from the Indian Military Academy, Dehradun, in 2018. Meanwhile, his wife Jyoti Saurot is a 2019 pass-out. Families met during a religious journey The groom's relatives say Madhur's parents had gone to Mathura on a religious journey. Jyoti's family members were also part of that journey. During the conversation, Jyoti's family mentioned that they were looking for a good match for their daughter. That's when Madhur's mother mentioned that her son is in government service. He is working as a Major in the army. After this, conversations between both families began, and gradually this relationship progressed to marriage. Mother-in-law says we consider her daughter, not daughter-in-law Major Madhur Chaudhary's mother, Rekha Chaudhary, says, ‘The daughter-in-law has come to my house like Goddess Lakshmi’. From day one, we have treated her not as a daughter-in-law, but like a daughter. We are very happy. The kind of life partner Madhur wanted for his son, he has found exactly such a daughter. We pray that their married life is always filled with happiness. Father-in-law says, ‘Daughter-in-law is more valuable than dowry’ Chaudhary Ompal Singh said that for us, the daughter-in-law is the biggest dowry. Many prestigious families approached for marriage, but they had already made a resolution to marry without dowry. Wealth comes and goes, but a cultured daughter connects two families. Major Madhur Chaudhary said that I had decided during my student life that I wouldn't take dowry. I made this decision after reading news about broken relationships and scattered families due to dowry. I also appeal to the youth to respect their parents' values. Come forward to bring positive change in society.

stories.title: Will Varun Gandhi get a new role after meeting Modi?:Absent from UP politics for two years, has not visited Pilibhit since 2024
stories.summary: Varun Gandhi entered politics and won the Pilibhit Lok Sabha seat in 2019. In 2014, he contested from Sultanpur and secured victory again by a margin of nearly 1.75 lakh votes. Just before the 2009 election, during a speech in Pilibhit, Varun made a controversial remark, stating that if anyone targeted Hindus or considered them leaderless, he would retaliate strongly, invoking the Gita. Statements like these significantly boosted his visibility in Uttar Pradesh, establishing him as a prominent Hindutva face. With the BJP forming the government at the Centre and Narendra Modi becoming Prime Minister, speculation intensified in Uttar Pradesh that Varun could emerge as Chief Minister if the party won the 2017 Assembly elections. Posters projecting him as a ‘future Chief Minister’ appeared in cities like Prayagraj. Sidelined after BJP’s rise in Uttar Pradesh Despite the BJP’s victory in 2017, Yogi Adityanath was appointed Chief Minister. Thereafter, Varun Gandhi’s political prominence gradually declined. By 2019, he was excluded from the list of star campaigners and removed from the party’s national executive. In 2024, he was denied a party ticket altogether, effectively halting his electoral political activity. On 17 March 2026, Varun met Prime Minister Modi, reigniting discussions about his political future. Questions are now being raised about whether he will be assigned a new role or fielded strategically against opposition leaders like Rahul Gandhi. Differences with party leadership Varun Gandhi has long been considered close to Rajnath Singh and reportedly favoured him as a prime ministerial candidate. During a rally in Kolkata addressed by Modi, Varun publicly criticised the crowd’s “Modi-Modi” chants, questioning their appropriateness. Although the rally was deemed successful, Varun described it as a failure the following day. After Modi became Prime Minister and Amit Shah replaced Rajnath Singh as BJP president, Varun’s position weakened. He was subsequently removed from the post of general secretary. Increasingly rebellious image Despite winning Pilibhit again in 2019, Varun adopted a more independent stance, often deviating from the party line. Four major incidents reinforced his image as a dissenter- Meeting with PM Modi On 17 March 2026, Varun shared a photograph with Prime Minister Modi, his wife Yamini Roy, and daughter Anasuya. He described the meeting as a privilege, praising Modi’s “paternal affection” and calling him a true guardian of the nation. Experts see an attempt at political rehabilitation Senior journalist Harshvardhan Tripathi views the meeting as an attempt by Varun Gandhi to regain political relevance. He argues that Varun had earlier opposed Modi through speeches and writings, especially during the farmers’ protests, even aligning with opposition narratives. Tripathi suggests Varun may have anticipated a decline in Modi’s political dominance by 2024. However, when that did not materialise, he was left with limited options. He also notes that Modi’s strategy often includes maintaining a Gandhi family member outside Congress, which serves as a symbolic counterpoint. However, experts believe Varun is unlikely to be given a major role in Uttar Pradesh ahead of the 2027 elections, though a position within the party structure remains possible. Internal factors behind marginalisation Journalist Keshav Agarwal highlights two key reasons for Varun’s sidelining- Congress option rejected At one stage, Varun explored joining Congress. However, Rahul Gandhi reportedly declined the proposal. Analysts suggest Rahul may have viewed Varun as a politically mature rival whose inclusion could complicate internal dynamics. Political legacy shaped by early loss Born on 13 March 1980 in Delhi, Varun Gandhi faced early personal tragedies. His father, Sanjay Gandhi, died in a plane crash when he was three months old. At age four, he lost his grandmother, former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi. Raised by Maneka Gandhi, Varun was introduced to politics in Pilibhit in 1999. He joined the BJP in 2004 and quickly rose through the ranks. Aggressive image and decline Between 2012 and 2017, during the Samajwadi Party government in Uttar Pradesh, Varun gained popularity through aggressive speeches, particularly in western UP and Rohilkhand. He even publicly rejected Mahatma Gandhi’s principle of non-violence in one speech. Although he built a strong support base, this assertive style, combined with internal dissent against party leadership, gradually distanced him from mainstream BJP politics. His recent meeting with Modi signals an attempt to reclaim lost ground in a rapidly evolving political landscape.

stories.title: President Droupadi Murmu visits Ayodhya:Offer prayers at Ram Temple and attend Shri Ram Yantra consecration ceremony
stories.summary: President Droupadi Murmu visited the Ram Temple in Ayodhya on the first day of Navratri, where she offered prayers to Ram Lalla. She also installed the Shri Ram Yantra in the Ram Darbar located on the second floor and took a round of the temple premises. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath briefed the President about the ongoing temple construction work. The President arrived at Ayodhya airport around 10:30 AM from Delhi, where she was received by Governor Anandiben Patel and the Chief Minister. This is the President’s second visit to Ayodhya after the consecration of Ram Lalla. Earlier, she had visited on May 1, 2024, when she offered prayers at Hanumangarhi and the Ram Temple. The President is scheduled to stay in Ayodhya for around five hours before leaving for Mathura at 3 PM. In Mathura, she will visit ISKCON and Prem Mandir. On Friday, March 20, she will meet Premanand Maharaj. During her visit, she performed aarti at the Ram Temple. Her granddaughters, Adyashree and Nityashree, also accompanied her to the temple and were seen offering prayers. The President also inspected the temple premises, while the Chief Minister shared details about the construction work. To welcome the President, cultural programmes were organised at 20 locations between the airport and the temple, with around 250 artists giving performances. About the Ram Yantra The Ram Yantra was prepared at a monastery in Kanchipuram, Tamil Nadu. It was then brought to Tirupati in Andhra Pradesh and later reached Ayodhya through a chariot procession about 10 days ago. The Yantra weighs around 150 kg and is plated with gold. According to Ayodhya astrologer Raghunath Das Shastri, the Ram Yantra is a special Vedic geometric structure. It symbolises divine energy, with the presence of Lord Ram and other deities established through sacred chants and patterns, and is considered highly auspicious.

stories.title: No tolerance for disruption during festivals, says CM Yogi:Police told to stay alert, increase patrolling, extra vigilance at crowded and religious places
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath said no disruption will be tolerated during festivals, warning of strict action against those attempting to disturb communal harmony. He stressed that criminals must fear the police uniform. The CM also directed that festivals be celebrated strictly within traditional norms, adding that no new practices will be allowed. These remarks came during a review meeting on preparations for Navratri and Eid, attended virtually by commissioners, district magistrates, and police chiefs on Wednesday evening. The DGP informed the Chief Minister that the police are fully alert to ensure the peaceful completion of the festivals. Patrolling has also been increased. Referring to recent criminal incidents, the CM said; Peace and security must be ensured at all costs. Negligence at any level will not be accepted. Even a single criminal incident spoils the atmosphere of the entire society. Therefore, every complaint and every incident should be taken seriously. Read CM's important statements On gas shortage says, ‘Keep strict watch on black marketing’ Regarding LPG supply, the CM said that despite international conditions, common people should not face any problems. Strict watch should be kept on hoarding and black marketing. Strict action should be taken against the culprits, and people's problems should be resolved immediately. 'Sound of loudspeakers at religious places should remain within set standards' Citing Supreme Court directions, Yogi said that the volume of loudspeakers at religious places should be kept within prescribed limits. Strict action should be taken to remove them if the rules are violated. Expressing displeasure over bike stunts, he directed them to stop it immediately. 'Exercise additional vigilance at major temples during Navratri' The Chief Minister said that during Chaitra Navratri, complete arrangements should be made for security, cleanliness, crowd management, drinking water, lighting, and health services, keeping in mind the crowd of devotees in Devi temples. Additional vigilance should be maintained at major temples and crowded areas. 'Cow shelter facilities will be improved' The Chief Minister directed to further improve the arrangements of destitute cow shelters. He asked to ensure the deployment of nodal officers, the timely payment of funds, the protection of cattle, fodder, and other necessary facilities.

stories.title: Storms hit Mathura-Sambhal; hoardings and trees fall:Drizzle in Ghaziabad, rain alert in 23 districts of UP
stories.summary: The weather has changed once again in UP. Late-night rain with storms occurred in Ghaziabad, Hathras, Sambhal, and Noida. In Mathura, strong winds knocked down hoardings on the road. Trees and electricity poles were also uprooted in many places. Standing crops have also been damaged. A house roof collapsed. Strong winds also blew in Sambhal. In Ghaziabad, it rained intermittently at night. There was also light drizzle on Thursday morning. The meteorological department estimates 3 millimeters of rainfall. The temperature here dropped by 4 degrees Celsius in 24 hours. Clouds have also been covering Noida since morning. The meteorological department has issued a rain alert with thunderstorms in 23 districts of the state today, Thursday. Hail is expected in 6 districts. During this time, winds can also blow at speeds of 40 to 60 km/h. According to the meteorological department, the weather will remain like this for the next 3 days till March 21. If we talk about Wednesday, Banda was the hottest, where the maximum temperature was recorded at 39.6 degrees. Dust storms occurred in Bulandshahr and Agra. Watch the visuals of storm and rain... Why did the weather change, know here Lucknow meteorologist Atul Singh said - A western disturbance has become active near Afghanistan from today. Its effect is visible up to UP. The weather has changed due to this. Its greater effect will be seen from March 20. Due to rain, the maximum temperature may drop by 5 to 7 degrees. How will the weather be for 3 days? March 20 - The effect of a western disturbance will be seen across the state. Many districts may experience rain with strong winds. There is also a possibility of hail. March 21 - There may be rain in some districts of Western-Eastern UP. Winds will blow at a speed of 40 km per hour. The temperature may drop by 2-3 degrees. March 22 - Most districts of Western-Eastern UP will remain cloudy. There may be rain in some places. Strong winds will also blow. Wheat and pigeon pea crops will be damaged. How can they be protected? Agricultural experts say that rain and strong winds can affect rabi, zaid, and horticultural crops. Currently, pods are forming in pigeon pea, mustard, chickpea, peas, green gram, and groundnut. Grains are filling. Strong winds can cause pods to split. Grains can fall off. Wheat crop can also fall due to strong winds, which poses a risk of reduced yield. In vegetables, flowers, and small fruits of okra, tomato, bottle gourd, cucumber, watermelon, muskmelon, eggplant, and chili can fall. Farmers have been advised to immediately harvest crops that are ripe and store them in a safe place. Do not let water accumulate in the fields; arrange proper drainage for this.

stories.title: 3 departments responsible for Green Corridor road collapse:Water line relocated; sewer line left untouched to cut costs
stories.summary: The Green Corridor road sank 5 feet due to sewer leakage just 2 days after inauguration in Lucknow. The road caved in near Khatu Shyam Temple on Birbal Sahani Marg. LDA officials kept insisting this was part of the ramp adjacent to the Green Corridor. However, Jal Kal department officials say that LDA was advised about sewer line shifting before the Green Corridor construction began. This was ignored due to rushed work and budget constraints. During construction, local residents had informed the construction workers about the leakage. Despite this, the sewer line was not fixed properly, while 2 drinking water lines were shifted. The Jal Kal department had not given any information about line shifting to Jal Nigam who was handling maintenance. There was a lack of coordination between all departments and officials. This negligence occurred as a result. Note that Defense Minister Rajnath Singh and Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath inaugurated the Green Corridor on March 13. The road caved in on March 15. These 3 are responsible for road cave-in... First - Lucknow Development Authority Phase-2 of the Green Corridor has been constructed by the Lucknow Development Authority. After the road collapsed, people told the Jal Nigam and Jalkal Department's working agency, Suez India, who arrived at the spot, that there was a leakage here when the road was being constructed. At that time, LDA did not pay attention to this and widened the road. Leakage occurred due to the compressor machine pressure After the road collapsed, the engineers working and local people said that when the compressor machine was running during road construction. The leakage occurred due to its pressure. Initially, the leakage was minor, but later it became larger. Due to which the road sank about 5 feet. The line had to be fixed by digging a hole about 20 feet deep. However, after the road collapsed, LDA said that it had nothing to do with corridor construction. A team led by Upper Secretary Gyanendra Verma also inspected and said that the green corridor is safe. Second - Jal Nigam Jal Nigam is responsible for the maintenance of sewer lines. Local residents told the officials who reached the spot that during road construction, they were informed about the leakage, but they did not pay attention. Due to this, a small problem became big. On the Jalkal department's advice regarding line shifting, Chief Engineer of Jal Nigam Shamim Akhtar said that Jal Nigam was not given any information in this matter. Two drinking water lines were shifted. Its proposal had also come. No information or proposal was provided by the Water Works Department regarding this. Only the Water Works GM had gone to the meeting held before making the corridor. Upon inquiring about the leakage, he said that the line runs under pressure in the rising line. Information is only known when water comes out. Regarding the cost of line shifting, officials say that if the line is crossing along with the road, the work gets done in a lower budget. If the line runs alongside, it costs more. Now, Jal Nigam will ask Sewage India to bring such equipment that can detect leakage in the rising main line. Third - Water works department Lucknow Jal Kal Department had advised LDA to shift the sewer line, but LDA ignored it in the rush of work. Meanwhile, Jal Nigam, which is looking after the maintenance work, said they have no information about any such proposal. In this situation, the question arises whether the Jal Kal department merely went through the motions in the name of giving advice for line shifting? Jal Kal department's GM Kuldeep Singh said that a large sewer line is going from the Kukrail pumping station. There was also a discussion about shifting this sewer line. However, due to it being a large line, the cost would be higher. Because of this, this proposal was postponed. Read now how the road will be built... LDA itself has to do the back-filling There was a gap in the pipeline joint in the Green Corridor, which caused water leakage. The Jal Nigam and Suez India teams have resolved the problem. Now, the Lucknow Development Authority will carry out the backfilling of this pit. Road construction will also be completed by the same department. Local residents have informed Suez India and Jal Nigam that when the road was being constructed, they had informed the working officers and employees about the water leakage. They were asked to inform the concerned department so that this problem could be resolved, but despite all this, the road construction work was carried out.

stories.title: First look of Asia's largest Noida Airport:Ganga Ghat-style entry and automatic baggage drop boxes
stories.summary: The Noida International Airport being built in Jewar, UP is ready for your journey. In the first phase, work on one terminal and runway built on 3300 acres has been completed. Only finishing remains. With one runway, this terminal will have an annual capacity to handle 30 million passengers. The cost of the airport's first phase is about 11 thousand crores. PM Modi will inaugurate it on 28 March. After completion of all 4 phases, it will be Asia's largest and world's sixth largest airport. However, the deadline for complete construction is 2040. Bhaskar is the first to reach inside this airport. Read all the important information... 1. Terminal Building 2. Entry Gate 3. Departure Area 4. Self Baggage Drop Facility 5. Security Check 6. Boarding Area 7. Lounge Area 8. Temple of Bells 9. Aerobridge 10. Security Special Features of Noida Airport 1. Asia's Largest Airport in Terms of Runways Noida International Airport will have 5 runways. A sixth runway may also be constructed here. After this, it will become Asia's largest and world's sixth largest airport. In terms of runways, China's Shanghai Pudong International Airport is currently the largest in Asia. 2. Also Asia's Largest in Terms of Area Noida International Airport is proposed to be built on a total area of 52 square kilometers. If this happens, it will become Asia's largest airport in terms of area as well. Currently, China's Beijing Daxing International Airport is Asia's largest airport with an area of 47 square kilometers. 3. Will be the country's largest airport after completion Yamuna Development Authority has allotted 3300 acres of land for the first stage of Noida Airport. This area is approximately 13.35 square kilometers. In the second stage, the total area of the airport will increase to about 7200 acres or 29 square kilometers. Currently, the country's largest airport is Rajiv Gandhi International Airport in Hyderabad, which is built on approximately 5500 acres or 22.25 square kilometers. Inauguration on March 28, First Flight in April PM Modi will inaugurate the Noida International Airport on March 28. However, flights will begin in April. Officials associated with the Noida Airport Authority said that fares have not been decided yet, but they could be lower compared to Delhi airport as the development charges for airlines have been kept lower here.

stories.title: Mother wanted euthanasia for Harish, father initially resisted:Brahmakumari's sister says his karmic journey is complete
stories.summary: 'You are like a bird trapped in a cage of sorrow and pain. The time has come for you to fly free.' These were the words of Brahmakumari Sister Lovely as she bid an emotional farewell to Harish Rana in Ghaziabad. Harish, who has been in a coma for 13 years, is currently at the All India Institute of Medical Sciences after the Supreme Court of India permitted passive euthanasia on his parents’ petition. Medical condition and current status Harish has been taken off oxygen support, and food and water have also been withheld for the past two days. Previously, he was being fed through a tube. A team of doctors at AIIMS is monitoring his condition continuously. Meanwhile, his parents remain in a hospital ward, praying for a peaceful and painless passing for their son. SC approval and transfer to AIIMS On 11 March, the Supreme Court granted permission for euthanasia. Subsequently, on 14 March, Harish was shifted from his residence in Raj Empire Society, Raj Nagar, Ghaziabad, to AIIMS Delhi. At the time of his departure, Sister Lovely, associated with the Brahmakumari organisation, offered spiritual support and performed a farewell ritual with the family. Family’s internal conflict over Euthanasia According to Sister Lovely, Harish’s father, Ashok Rana, was initially opposed to euthanasia, believing in a natural death. However, his mother, Nirmala, had a different perspective. She had expressed her wish for euthanasia nearly four years ago, stating that she could no longer bear to see her son’s suffering. She sought Sister Lovely’s help in convincing her husband. Over time, with counselling and emotional support, the father and other family members came to accept the decision. The family then pursued legal recourse, taking the matter from the High Court to the Supreme Court. Long association with Brahmakumaris Sister Lovely stated that the Rana family had been associated with the Prajapita Brahmakumari Ishwariya Vishwavidyalaya for 18 years. About five years ago, they began attending daily one-hour classes at her centre in Rajnagar Extension, which strengthened their connection. It was during this association that she became personally involved in the family’s struggle and their eventual decision regarding euthanasia. Harish’s condition over the years Sister Lovely described Harish as a “pure soul” whose karmic journey had been fulfilled. Despite being in a coma, his eyes often remained open, and he occasionally coughed or showed minor responses. However, there was no movement in the rest of his body. Over the years, his physical condition deteriorated severely. His body became extremely frail, with bones visibly protruding. His parents and younger brother Ashish cared for him tirelessly, even helping him sit upright at times. Emotional moments before transfer A video from 14 March shows Sister Lovely applying a sandalwood tilak on Harish’s forehead and gently telling him to forgive everyone and seek forgiveness before departing. Family members were visibly emotional. Harish’s father apologised to relatives, saying he was taking this step despite personal reluctance. Family’s struggle and silence The Rana family moved to Ghaziabad about six years ago, after previously living in Delhi for over a decade. Since Harish’s transfer to AIIMS, a deep silence has enveloped the household. Neighbours say the father has withdrawn from social interactions. Harish’s mother and sister continue to grieve, recalling years of caregiving. His mother shared how she would speak to him daily, hoping for even the slightest response, a blink, a yawn, or a twitch, just to feel he was still present. Accident and diagnosis Harish, originally from Delhi, was pursuing a B.Tech at Punjab University in Chandigarh. In 2013, during his final semester, he fell from the fourth floor of his hostel. The accident left him paralysed and in a coma. Doctors diagnosed him with Quadriplegia, a condition in which survival often depends on ventilatory and assisted feeding support. Recovery chances in such cases are extremely limited. Over time, prolonged immobility also led to severe bedsores, further worsening his condition, making the family’s emotional and physical burden increasingly difficult to bear.

Not advocacy, but open hooliganism:Supreme Court slams Barabanki toll clash; calls lawyer ‘brave’ who represented toll workers
stories.summary: 'The behavior of Barabanki Bar Association members is extremely sad and shameful. This is not the legal profession, but open hooliganism. This incident shows the declining state of the legal profession. Such violence can never be acceptable in the name of lawyers' fraternity (brotherhood).' This stern comment was made by the Supreme Court regarding a case related to a dispute at a toll plaza in Barabanki. The bench of Justice Vikram Nath and Justice Sandeep Mehta ordered the transfer of the entire case from Barabanki to Delhi's Tis Hazari Court. The Supreme Court also praised lawyer Manoj Shukla, who fought the case despite pressure. Now know complete matter On January 14, 2026, a dispute over toll occurred between lawyer Ratnesh Shukla and toll workers at Haidargarh toll plaza in Barabanki. The toll workers had assaulted lawyer Ratnesh Shukla. A video of this incident had also surfaced. After the incident, lawyers began protesting against the toll workers. The District Bar Association had passed a resolution that no lawyer would represent the toll workers. Meanwhile, lawyer Manoj Shukla had filed a bail petition for toll workers opposing this proposal. Angered by this, some lawyers entered his chamber and vandalized and set it on fire. They also burned his effigy. When legal assistance was not available at the local level, the toll workers went to the Supreme Court. Supreme Court made strong remarks During the hearing of this case, the Supreme Court bench, which included Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta, expressed strong displeasure over the attitude of the Barabanki Bar Association. The court said that such incidents reflect the declining reputation of the judicial system and legal profession. Additionally, the court praised Manoj Shukla, calling him a 'brave lawyer' who fought the case despite pressure. The Supreme Court granted bail to the toll plaza employees. Also, directed the UP DGP to ensure their security. They should be escorted to a safe location. Case transferred from UP to Delhi Due to violence and local protests by lawyers, the court transferred the entire case from UP to Delhi. The Supreme Court said that the legal rights of toll workers were affected because no lawyer was willing to stand in their favor. UP Bar Council also reprimanded The Supreme Court also reprimanded the Uttar Pradesh Bar Council. Said that the Council's demand to impose NSA from the state government was inappropriate, as it was a case of minor scuffle. The court expressed hope that the Bar Council of India will take necessary action in this entire matter.

stories.title: Aparna Yadav writes to CM Yogi against rapper Badshah:Seeks ban on show; says women insulted in 'Tateeree' song
stories.summary: Rapper Badshah has started facing opposition in UP after Haryana. Aparna Yadav, Vice President of the Women's Commission, wrote a letter to CM Yogi Adityanath on Thursday. She has demanded a ban on Badshah's stage shows in UP. Aparna wrote in the letter: Badshah's new song 'Tateeree' uses abusive language towards women. Objectionable scenes have been shown. Sacred places like schools have also been addressed with derogatory words. This has severely insulted the dignity of women. Aparna Yadav said - In the song, female students in school uniforms have been shown inappropriately. This hurts the dignity of women and social values. Demand for issuing a lookout circular Information has also been received about an FIR being registered and a lookout circular being issued in this matter. The Chief Minister is requested to instruct all district magistrates of the state to cancel permission for any proposed program of singer Badshah. First, know why there is a controversy over the song Show to be held in Pilibhit on March 20 In Pilibhit, a 2-hour non-stop live magic show/concert named "Badshah Magic World" is scheduled for March 20. The show promises family entertainment with digital magic like mind reading, telepathy, and live dinosaurs. After Aparna Yadav wrote a letter to the Chief Minister, there is now confusion regarding the organization of this event. Haryana Women's Commission also summoned Amidst the controversy, the Haryana Women's Commission had issued a notice to Badshah last Friday. He has been asked to appear in Panipat on March 13. Additionally, 3 separate cases have been registered against the singer in Panchkula and Jind. Khap panchayats and social organisations had also demanded a ban on this song, calling it against Haryanvi culture.

Adarsh is a Navy personnel in the Indian Navy and is accused of spying for Pakistan’s intelligence agency ISI. 3. UP woman’s IAS claim turns fake: Celebrated securing 113th rank in UPSC 2025 After Bihar’s Akanksha, a similar case has surfaced in Uttar Pradesh, where Shikha Gautam’s claim of becoming an IAS officer in the UPSC-2025 results has turned out to be false. 6. Suspended IAS officer reinstated in ₹1 crore bribery case The Uttar Pradesh government has reinstated suspended IAS officer Abhishek Prakash after nearly a year. He had earlier been accused of demanding a commission of ₹1 crore from businessman Vishwajeet Dutta through his close aide. 7. Rahul Gandhi claims the Petroleum Minister called Epstein a friend Opposition created an uproar in the Lok Sabha today over the LPG cylinder crisis in the country. As soon as proceedings began at 11 am, members started raising slogans. 8. Black marketing of LPG cylinders begins in Lucknow: Being sold for ₹1,600–₹3,500 The shortage of LPG gas cylinders in Lucknow is continuously increasing. Due to the disrupted supply of both domestic and commercial cylinders, people associated with the hotel. 9. Akhilesh Yadav meets Shankaracharya in Lucknow SP chief Akhilesh Yadav met Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand in Lucknow on Thursday. Akhilesh greeted the saints present there with folded hands at the entrance. Former MP Anu Tandon was also present with him. 10. Travelling by Air India Group flights is becoming expensive Considering the increase in jet fuel (ATF) prices owing to the oil supply disruptions caused by the US-Israel and Iran war, Indian aviation companies will increase fares even further in the coming days.

stories.title: 2 HPCL officers shot dead in UP:Gunman enters plant with automatic weapon, kills DGM and manager
stories.summary: Two senior officials of Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited (HPCL) were shot dead inside a company plant in Uttar Pradesh’s Budaun on Thursday afternoon, allegedly by a dismissed former employee who had been holding a grudge against the management. The victims were identified as Sudhir Gupta (55), Deputy General Manager (DGM), and Harshit Mishra (40), Assistant Manager (Sales). Police said the accused, Ajay Pratap Singh alias Ramu Singh, a former vendor and employee associated with the plant, opened fire at the officials during a meeting inside the premises around 1 pm. Accused entered plant in Bolero, opened rapid fire According to initial information, Ajay Pratap Singh arrived at the plant in a Bolero vehicle along with five others, including four plant employees and a driver. The group reportedly entered the premises before the employees’ shift, which was scheduled to begin at 2 pm. Officials said the vehicle was not checked at the plant gate, allowing the accused to enter with an automatic firearm. Shortly after entering, Ajay allegedly began arguing with the officers and suddenly opened rapid fire at Sudhir Gupta and Harshit Mishra. Both officials sustained critical gunshot injuries and collapsed on the spot. They were rushed to the Dataganj Community Health Centre (CHC), where doctors declared them dead. See 3 visuals related to the incident... Police seal plant, investigation underway Following the incident, police sealed the plant premises and stopped the entry of visitors. Senior police and administrative officers rushed to the spot after receiving information about the double murder. DIG Ajay Sahni reached the plant and supervised the investigation. Police teams have begun questioning staff members present during the incident. Security has also been tightened at the HPCL plant, Dataganj CHC, and the district hospital as a precautionary measure. Eyewitnesses: accused forced entry, fired after argument Eyewitnesses said that Ajay Pratap Singh, a resident of Sainjani village, forcibly entered the plant with several people around 1 pm. He allegedly began abusing associates of the two officers. When Sudhir Gupta and Harshit Mishra objected, the situation escalated. In the middle of the argument, Ajay reportedly pulled out a firearm and began shooting. The accused fled the scene immediately after firing the shots. Earlier dispute and threats Investigators say the attack may be linked to an earlier dispute at the plant on February 5. Police said Ajay Pratap Singh had created a disturbance at the facility that day by breaking through the security perimeter and entering the premises forcibly. Following the incident, the company terminated his contract and barred him from the plant. Officials said he was also blacklisted three months ago, which allegedly fuelled his resentment. According to police, Ajay had openly threatened to kill DGM Sudhir Gupta during the earlier confrontation. Witnesses claimed he had also boasted of links with notorious gangster groups in Noida and Shahjahanpur, showing knife scars on his body and warning that he would “teach everyone a lesson”. After the February dispute, the accused allegedly followed the officers’ vehicles for nearly five kilometres, repeatedly overtaking them and issuing threats. Assistant Manager Harshit Mishra had filed an FIR against him in connection with that incident. Victim’s background Sudhir Gupta was originally from Silver Estate Apartment, Sector 50, Noida. His father’s name is Dayakishan. At the time of the incident, Gupta was residing near Sanjay Community in Bareilly due to his posting. Accused arrested Senior Superintendent of Police Dr Brajesh Singh said the shooting took place while officials were attending a meeting inside the HPCL plant. “During the meeting, a former vendor of the plant entered the premises and opened fire. The injured officials were immediately taken to hospital, where they were declared dead. The accused has been arrested,” the SSP said. Police said further investigation is underway to determine whether others present in the vehicle were aware of the attack plan or involved in the crime.

stories.title: Need a gas cylinder? Don’t panic:Officials claim a 25-day reserve stock across the state, even if the war escalates
stories.summary: Images of panic buying of gas cylinders are emerging from different cities of Uttar Pradesh. Gas supply is being carried out in the presence of police. Even people who do not immediately need cylinders are booking them. The government has already stopped the supply of commercial gas cylinders. Because of this, many people fear that the supply of domestic cylinders may also be affected. How valid is this concern? What preparations have petroleum companies made for the next six months? Can cylinder prices increase? Dainik Bhaskar explains answers to nine key questions. Question 1: Can there be a shortage of domestic cylinders? Answer: Due to the Iran war, uncertainty has arisen regarding gas and crude oil. Gas supply has been disrupted by up to 30%. Because of this, the Petroleum Ministry has fixed supply priorities. The government has reduced commercial gas supply by 20–30%. Agencies are now focusing on supplying domestic LPG cylinders. Through this system, the government aims to ensure 100% availability of domestic gas and CNG for the next six months. Question 2: How many days of reserve stock does the government have? Answer: There is no shortage of LPG cylinders. Refineries have increased LPG production by around 10%. Officials say there is no need to panic. Gas companies are sending messages to customers saying claims of gas shortage are misleading. Food and Civil Supplies Principal Secretary Ranveer Prasad said, “There is a reserve stock of domestic LPG cylinders for 20 to 25 days in Uttar Pradesh.” Question 3: Will cylinders not be available even after 26 days in the coming period? Answer: Food and Civil Supplies Principal Secretary Ranveer Prasad said, “Because of panic booking, demand suddenly increased. Therefore, on March 6, oil companies introduced a 21-day lock-in period for domestic LPG booking.” He added, “Lock-in period means that after delivery of one cylinder, a new cylinder can be booked only after 21 days. On March 9, the lock-in period was increased to 25 days.” “The automatic booking system has been updated accordingly. That is why gas agencies are unable to accept bookings earlier. There is little possibility of any change in the lock-in period in the coming days,” he said. Question 4: Should people panic? Answer: Before the Iran–Israel war, there was no lock-in period. People could book a new cylinder on the same day the previous one was delivered. Now that this is not possible, an atmosphere of panic has developed among people. However, officials say there is no need to panic. Question 5: Why has the government implemented the Essential Commodities Act? Answer: The Essential Commodities Act gives the government the power to control supply and prices of essential items such as grains, pulses, edible oils, medicines and fuel. In simple terms, it is a law to prevent hoarding. Under this law, traders are given a stock limit and cannot store goods beyond that limit in warehouses. This will also prevent black marketing of gas cylinders. In Gorakhpur’s Pipiganj area, two youths standing in a queue for cylinders at an Indane gas agency got into a fight. Police had to intervene to separate them. Question 6: What is the government doing to tackle gas shortage complaints? Answer: Complaints of LPG and petrol-diesel shortages have been reported from several districts of Uttar Pradesh. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath reviewed the situation on March 10. He instructed all District Magistrates and Superintendents of Police to monitor the situation in their respective districts. In major districts such as Noida, Lucknow, Kanpur and Prayagraj, the administration is inspecting gas depots and agencies to check whether any artificial shortage of gas or fuel is being created. Question 7: After booking, how many days does it take to receive a cylinder? Answer: Food and Civil Supplies Principal Secretary Ranveer Prasad said, “There is no district where gas supply has stopped.” “After booking, the standard supply time is seven days. However, in Uttar Pradesh, cylinders are being delivered to homes within two to three days. Around 8 to 10 lakh cylinders are delivered every day,” he said. Question 8: If the Iran–Israel war intensifies, will gas supply be affected? Answer: The government has already prepared for such a situation. Refineries have been asked to increase production. The Reliance refinery in Jamnagar and the HMEL refinery in Bathinda have been directed to stop petrol production and shift to gas production. After operating at full capacity, it is estimated that about 70% of the country’s requirement can be met. Question 9: Where can people complain if agencies are not delivering cylinders? Answer: A toll-free number has been issued for complaints. Consumers can call 1800-2333-555, which is common for Indane, Bharat Gas and HP Gas customers. Complaints can also be registered online at mylpg.in. (All answers were provided by Food and Civil Supplies Principal Secretary Ranveer Prasad.)

stories.summary: UP Panchayat Chunav 2026: यूपी पंचायत चुनाव कब होंगे? यूपी ग्राम प्रधान का चुनाव कब होंगे?… ये सवाल इस वक्त यूपी के हर एक गांव में सुनाई दे रहा है। आम जनता यूपी में होने वाले पंचायत चुनाव को लेकर सवाल कर रही है कि आखिर सरकार कब कराएगी चुनाव। पंचायत चुनाव में भाग लेने वाले प्रत्याशी परेशान हैं कि आखिर सरकार यूपी पंचायत चुनाव क्यों नहीं करा रही है। वहीं सरकार ने इसको लेकर OBC आयोग का गठन तक नहीं किया। उम्मीद थी कि 10 मार्च को होने वाले कैबिनेट बैठक में यूपी पंचायत चुनाव पर मोहर लग जाएगी, लेकिन इसको लेकर कोई चर्चा ही नहीं हुई। बता दें कि कोर्ट ने योगी सरकार को 2 फरवरी को OBC आयोग का गठन करने के लिए 15 दिन का समय दिया था, लेकिम लगभग 2 महीने से उपर का समय बीत चुका है और सरकार अभी तक आयोग का गठन नहीं कर पाई है। वहीं पंचायती राज मंत्री ओपी राजभर बार-बार पंचायत चुनाव समय पर कराने का दावा करते हैं, लेकिन अब ऐसा नहीं लगता कि यूपी पंचायत चुनाव समय पर हो पाएंगे। वहीं यूपी के डिप्टी सीएम ने एक ऐसा बयान दे दिया है, जिसके बाद यह साफ हो गया है कि यूपी पंचायत चुनाव समय पर बिल्कुल भी नहीं कराए जाएंगे।

stories.title: Massive fire at Noida factory:Firefighters climb roof, break windows to rescue 35 workers; many carried out on shoulders
stories.summary: A massive fire broke out at an electricity meter manufacturing factory in Noida on Thursday, triggering panic among workers and prompting a large rescue operation by the fire department. The fire started suddenly at the Capital Power System Limited factory located in the Phase-1 police station area. Within minutes, the flames spread rapidly across all five floors of the building. More than 200 employees managed to run out of the factory to save their lives. However, around 35 workers were trapped inside, many of whom reportedly lost consciousness due to smoke. Local residents alerted the police and the fire department soon after the fire broke out. More than 30 fire tenders rushed to the spot and began rescue and firefighting operations. Firefighters used ladders to reach the first-floor balcony and broke the glass windows to enter the building. Rescue teams then brought the trapped workers down on their shoulders and shifted them to safety. The injured were taken to the district hospital by the police and emergency teams. Officials said most of the workers suffered minor injuries, mainly due to smoke inhalation and panic. However, two workers suffered serious burn injuries. One of them has been referred to a hospital in Delhi for advanced treatment. Firefighters battled the blaze for several hours before bringing it under control. Officials said it took around four to five hours to fully control the fire. 5 Pictures of the Accident... Short circuit suspected behind Noida factory fire; smoke visible 2 km away A short circuit is suspected to have caused the massive fire that broke out at an electricity meter manufacturing factory in Noida early Thursday morning, officials said. According to initial reports, the fire started on the ground floor around 5.30 am. Due to the large quantity of plastic components and electrical wiring materials stored inside the factory, the flames spread rapidly through the building. The blaze was so intense that thick clouds of smoke were visible from nearly two kilometres away, creating panic in the surrounding areas. During the chaos, one employee suffered a fractured leg while trying to escape from the burning building. He was rushed to hospital and is currently undergoing treatment. Police and emergency teams shifted all the injured workers to the district hospital in ambulances. Most of the employees sustained minor injuries, while some were treated for smoke inhalation. Firefighters used powerful water jets and continued operations for several hours before bringing the blaze under control. After the flames were contained, rescue teams carried out a thorough search of the factory building to ensure that no one was left trapped inside. Officials later confirmed that no additional workers were found inside the factory during the search operation. Joint Commissioner of Police (Law and Order) Rajeev Narayan Mishra said that authorities responded quickly after receiving information about the incident. “This morning, information was received about a fire in a factory located in Sector-4. The local police and fire brigade team immediately reached the spot and the fire has been brought under control,” he said. Authorities are now investigating the incident and assessing the extent of damage caused to the factory.
