stories.title: Sambhal CO warns against protests over Iran–Israel conflict:Says, 'anyone disturbing peace during Eid or raising slogans over foreign issues will face strict police action'
stories.summary: Circle Officer Kuldeep Kumar made the remarks during a Peace Committee meeting held in the Asmoli area of Sambhal district. Referring to the ongoing Iran-Israel conflict, he said that some people appear overly concerned about the issue and warned them not to create disturbances locally over international matters. He added that if anyone has such strong feelings about the conflict, they should go and support the country they favour instead of disturbing peace here. He also warned that the police would take strict action against anyone attempting to disrupt law and order. A video of the meeting has also surfaced. The meeting was organised at Sambhal Kotwali on Wednesday ahead of Alvida Jumma and Eid. Since the regular CO of Sambhal is on leave, Kuldeep Kumar was also handling the charge. City Magistrate Sudhir Kumar and Inspector Gajendra Singh were present during the meeting. During the discussion, the officer appealed to members of the Muslim community to celebrate the festivals peacefully and emphasised that the city’s peace should not be disturbed in the name of international conflicts. Read what else the CO said Go board the plane going to Iran CO Kuldeep Kumar says, ‘Some people are very troubled here by the Iran-Israel war’. They are beating their chests here. If you have so many problems, then get on a plane and go there. These are all international issues. We don't need to get involved in what's happening in Bangladesh? Khamenei was killed in Iran? Sir, America is committing atrocities? Look, there are 56 Islamic countries; they will take care of themselves. If prayers are offered on the road, they will not be forgiven CO says, ‘When there is no space in the mosque, worshippers rush and start praying on the road’. If this happens, we won't say anything for one minute. After that, we will file a case and send them to jail. If anyone shows support or raises slogans for the Iran-Israel war, they will be sent to jail. If disputes from another country affect our country's law and order, the police will give a 'very good treatment'. During prayers, there should be no slogans, banners, or strips against any other country. Kuldeep Kumar says, ‘We are Hindustani, we are Indian’. We are living here peacefully. International issues are for governments to handle, not for common people. If 10 people are standing somewhere beating their chests saying Iran has been killed, then brothers go there and fight. Action will also be taken where posters are made The CO warned that police will take action not only against protesters but also at places where these controversial posters and slogans are printed or written. We are living here peacefully. No one will be allowed to spoil the atmosphere on their own land. The festival is about love and harmony. It's a festival of sweet vermicelli. No bitterness should be mixed in it. Don't let anyone in your area do anything that would spoil the environment. Strict action against REEL makers on social media CO warned social media reel makers, saying, ‘some people say anything just to make Instagram reels’. They spread rumors about issues in foreign countries. Such things will not be tolerated at all. We should not be concerned about what is happening in other countries. Those are their issues, not ours. We must not let our area's atmosphere get spoiled. One 'mischievous' person is enough to spoil the entire environment. Therefore, all responsible citizens should remain alert and cooperate with the police. The meeting was attended by council member Ibrahim, council member's husband Azeem Abbasi, Haji Ehtesham, and Mo. Nazim, Danish Khan, Mohammad Zia, Nabeel Ahmad, Shabban Khan, Akhtar, Idrees, Rashid, along with many other prominent people of the district. Around 50 people participated in the meeting. AIMIM UP President says, ‘Your language is like a street criminal.’ AIMIM's UP President Shaukat Ali has reacted to CO Kuldeep Kumar's statement in Sambhal. He says, ‘CO Kuldeep Kumar is making threats in the peace committee meeting’. If we do anything that is unconstitutional, then file a case. You are sitting and threatening Muslims. The first case should be filed against you. He said that you have considered Muslims weak. Everyone will come and threaten Muslims and leave. Earlier, CO Anuj Chaudhary did the same thing. He shot Muslims. He became a hero. Shaukat Ali says, 'It doesn't seem from anywhere that you have taken the oath of the Constitution'. Your language doesn't sound like an IPS officer's language; it sounds like the language of a street criminal. CO, sir, if you have a problem with us, then you go to Nepal.

The board will announce the method for declaring results for these students separately.

Strikes in Kandahar: Pakistan says it hit military facilities inside Afghanistan, attacks tunnel used by Taliban
stories.summary: Pakistan launched strikes on Afghan military facilities and alleged terrorist hideouts in Kandahar, escalating tensions with the Taliban. These actions follow Pakistan's interception of drone attacks originating from Afghanistan. The Taliban administration reported limited civilian damage, while Pakistan warned of retaliation after its president stated a "red line" was crossed by targeting civilians.

stories.title: Middle East War Day 16: UAE and other Gulf countries report fresh attacks; Kuwait airport hit
stories.summary: Explosions rocked Dubai as Iran claimed missile and drone strikes on the UAE's Al Dhafra airbase. Kuwait International Airport also reported drone impacts damaging radar, though no injuries occurred. These actions follow Iran's warnings and accusations of UAE ports being used for attacks on its oil facilities, escalating regional tensions.

stories.title: From Bridgerton balls to fake shaadis: How theme parties are the new rage
stories.summary: Theme parties are transforming social gatherings into immersive experiences, driven by social media and a desire for participation. Brands are engineering these events to foster deeper engagement, turning passive fandom into collective celebration. This trend taps into psychological needs for connection and belonging, creating shared cultural moments that extend beyond mere entertainment.

stories.title: Nepal bus accident: 7 Indian pilgrims killed, several injured after vehicle plunges into valley
stories.summary: Tragedy struck in Nepal as a passenger bus carrying Indian pilgrims veered off a mountain road, plunging into a valley. At least seven Indians lost their lives, with nine others injured. The pilgrims were returning from the revered Manakamana Temple when the devastating accident occurred near Shahid Lakhan village.

stories.title: Formula 1 cancels Bahrain and Saudi Arabia Grands Prix amid Middle East tensions; season cut to 22 races
stories.summary: Formula 1 and the FIA have cancelled the Bahrain and Saudi Arabian Grands Prix scheduled for April 2026 due to escalating Middle East conflict. Safety concerns and logistical challenges prompted the decision, impacting the 2026 calendar and creating a five-week gap before the Miami Grand Prix.

stories.title: UAE crackdown: 25 arrested for spreading misleading content and glorifying military aggression
stories.summary: UAE authorities have ordered the arrest of 25 individuals accused of spreading fabricated online content that could jeopardize national defense and incite panic. Investigations revealed these suspects, from various nationalities, used digital platforms to circulate manipulated footage and narratives related to regional tensions, leading to expedited trial proceedings.

Saudi Arabia umrah visa deadlines announced: Key dates for Pilgrims entry and exit, all you need to know

The ministry met with Umrah companies to discuss compliance for the upcoming Hajj season and praised their Ramadan efforts. Preparations for the Umrah and Visit Forum 2026 were also reviewed.

stories.title: Election Commission likely to announce assembly polls schedule for five states
stories.summary: The Election Commission is set to announce the schedule for assembly elections in West Bengal, Assam, Tamil Nadu, Kerala, and Puducherry today. The upcoming polls are expected to involve fewer phases, particularly in West Bengal, with a substantial increase in central forces deployment. Supplementary voter lists for West Bengal will also be published following the adjudication of 'doubtful' voter cases.

stories.title: FPV drones enter Iran vs US-Israel war: All about the low-cost ‘kamikaze’ weapons
stories.summary: The ongoing war between the United States, Israel, and Iran highlights the growing role of inexpensive drones. First-person-view (FPV) drones, originally for recreation, are now battlefield weapons. These agile drones offer precise strikes at a low cost, challenging expensive air defense systems. Their widespread use signals a shift in modern warfare tactics.

The demand reflects broader uncertainty about Washington’s objectives, exposing the limits of military force and the persistence of geopolitical and civilisational tensions in the post–Cold War world.

This comes as President Trump ordered the release of related files, though agencies are scrambling with no clear timeline. The expert anticipates some compelling data but doubts confirmation of alien contact.

stories.title: Marriage proposal cancelled: HIV-positive man injects infected blood into woman in Hyderabad
stories.summary: A 24-year-old man allegedly injected HIV-infected blood into his 22-year-old relative in Hyderabad after her family cancelled their wedding upon discovering his positive status. The incident occurred on March 11, with police stating the accused forcibly administered the blood. He has been apprehended, and the woman is hospitalized.

stories.title: Who is Dana Tran? Sean Diddy Combs’ former partner now linked to Desmond Scott after TMZ spending time report
stories.summary: Dana Tran, the former partner of Sean “Diddy” Combs and mother of his youngest child, is rumored to be dating influencer Desmond Scott. TMZ reported that the two have recently been spending time together, though sources say the relationship is not serious. Tran, known online as Dana Tee, has a background in cybersecurity and usually keeps her personal life private.

stories.title: Nearly 100 stray dogs poisoned to death in Telangana village
stories.summary: Nearly 100 stray dogs were allegedly poisoned to death in Telangana's Mancherial district, with an animal welfare activist filing a complaint against village officials. Police have registered a case under relevant acts, investigating allegations of hired individuals administering poisonous injections and burying the animals. This incident follows a pattern of mass canine killings reported in Telangana last year.

stories.title: Middle East crisis Day 15: Iran hits US embassy in Baghdad, UAE oil hub struck
stories.summary: The US-Israel conflict with Iran escalated significantly on its 15th day. Iran targeted the US embassy in Baghdad and a UAE oil hub, while Israel struck Lebanon and Iraq. Debris from intercepted missiles hit Dubai twice. The war now directly impacts diplomatic sites and oil infrastructure across the Gulf, with UAE intercepting over 1,800 Iranian projectiles.

stories.title: Queen Camilla believed Meghan ‘brainwashed’ Harry; Duke of Sussex ignored old friends and changed his phone number, new royal book claims

The book also details a tense meeting between the Sussexes and the Prince and Princess of Wales, and claims Meghan exploited the Invictus Games for personal gain.

stories.title: 'Yet another act of aggression': India condemns Pakistan air strikes in Afghanistan
stories.summary: India has strongly condemned Pakistan's airstrikes in Afghanistan, labeling them an "act of aggression" and emphasizing the need to respect Afghanistan's sovereignty. Pakistan claims its operations target Pakistani Taliban militants and their support networks.

Punjab: Amit Shah rules out Akali alliance revival, says BJP will fight 2027 polls to form own government
stories.summary: Union Home Minister Amit Shah declared the BJP will contest the 2027 Punjab Assembly elections independently, aiming to form its own government. He asserted the party's growing vote share and criticized the AAP government's performance on law and order, drugs, and corruption. Shah also pledged to enact a law against religious conversions if the BJP wins.

stories.title: Wanted fugitive killed by Dallas police reportedly worked as security guard for Jasmine Crockett: Report
stories.summary: A man known as Mike King, who provided security for US Rep. Jasmine Crockett and managed off-duty police work, was killed by Dallas police. Authorities stated he was wanted for impersonating an officer and barricaded himself in a vehicle. King's alleged use of aliases and a criminal history have raised significant questions.

stories.title: Iran crisis: MEA says five Indians killed, one missing in conflict; two LPG vessels cross Strait of Hormuz safely
stories.summary: Tragedy strikes as five Indians lose their lives and one remains missing amid escalating Middle East conflict. Meanwhile, two Indian LPG carriers have successfully navigated the Strait of Hormuz, en route to India with vital fuel supplies. Missions are working tirelessly to aid affected nationals and ensure repatriation.

stories.summary: Indian LPG vessels safely navigated the Strait of Hormuz amid Middle East tensions, with the government assuring all Indian crew are secure. Despite panic booking, LPG supplies remain stable. Climate activist Sonam Wangchuk was released after his NSA detention was revoked.

stories.title: 'Openly protecting rapists': PM Modi slams TMC over RG Kar and Sandeshkhali cases
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi launched a strong attack on the TMC in Kolkata, accusing the party of protecting rapists and insulting President Droupadi Murmu. He also alleged that the TMC opposes electoral roll revisions to shield infiltrators and deliberately alters demographics, making Hindus a minority in several areas.

stories.title: Tamil Nadu CM MK Stalin offers Rs 2 per unit power subsidy for eateries switching from LPG amid supply crisis
stories.summary: Tamil Nadu is offering a Rs 2 per unit electricity subsidy for restaurants and food businesses switching from LPG to electric stoves, aiming to mitigate fuel shortage impacts. The state also provides subsidized loans for electric equipment and allows industries temporary use of alternative fuels. Measures are in place to support farmers and monitor LPG distribution.

stories.title: 'I apologise': Trump aide Laura Loomer apologises for 'anti-India' posts on social media
stories.summary: Far-right activist Laura Loomer apologised for "anti-India" social media posts after facing backlash for racist remarks. While she expressed regret for offending people, Loomer stood firm on her opposition to the H-1B visa program, citing a need to protect American workers. She also criticized Pakistan, accusing it of supporting extremist networks.

stories.title: UAE News: Dubai Global Village cancels Eid Al Fitr fireworks, remains closed until further notice
stories.summary: Dubai's Global Village will not have its usual Eid Al Fitr fireworks this year. The popular attraction remains closed due to safety precautions. This decision follows country-wide directives restricting fireworks and drone shows. The closure is linked to heightened regional tensions. Authorities are prioritizing safety as the region navigates current geopolitical situations. Visitors should check official channels for updates.

stories.title: India’s Nobel Prize paradox: A long gap for laureates and why Mahatma Gandhi remains the most famous non-winner
stories.summary: Despite India's rich intellectual tradition and early Nobel laureates like Tagore and Raman, the country has experienced long gaps in recognition. Factors like brain drain, limited funding, and an emphasis on publications over long-term innovation hinder the journey from research to global acclaim. The case of Mahatma Gandhi's missed Peace Prize also highlights complexities beyond merit.

stories.title: TMC and BJP supporters clash in Kolkata hours before PM Modi’s rally
stories.summary: Tensions flared near Girish Park in Kolkata as TMC and BJP supporters clashed, pelting stones and raising slogans just before Prime Minister Modi's rally. Both parties accused each other of initiating the violence, with claims of damaged vehicles and hurled abuses. Police intervened to restore order in the area.

stories.title: How Ukraine trip unravelled Banksy's 'true identity'
stories.summary: For decades, the art world pondered the identity of Banksy, the anonymous street artist. Patient reporting, tracing clues from Bristol to Ukraine and a New York police file, revealed Robin Gunningham as the likely individual behind the iconic stencils. This discovery, while dismantling a myth, underscores the power of anonymity in art.

stories.title: Ladakh climate activist Sonam Wangchuk released from jail as govt revokes NSA detention

Wangchuk was detained over allegations of inciting unrest in Ladakh, with the government citing his remarks as potentially destabilizing. His wife had challenged the detention in the Supreme Court.

stories.summary: The UAE Cyber Security Council has issued a critical alert regarding the escalating threat of wiper malware, a destructive software designed to permanently delete data and cripple systems.
